Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Consumer Non-Cyclicals delivered a robust earnings expansion, with an average annual earnings growth of 42.03%, positioning the sector fifth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. Revenue grew more modestly at an average annual rate of 4.96%, which places the sector ninth in revenue growth rankings. Within the sector, [#VC2]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2] posted the strongest earnings increase, while [#EB5]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5] recorded the highest revenue growth. Growth is further shaped by Singapore’s reliance on imported food and the government’s emphasis on food security, which drives demand for locally sourced agricultural products and supports firms that can enhance supply chain resilience. These sector-specific dynamics help explain the strong earnings momentum despite slower revenue growth.
Consumer Cyclicals: Despite a modest decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of just under one percent, the Consumer Cyclicals sector posted a robust revenue expansion of about fifteen percent over the past year. This earnings performance places the sector twelfth out of fifteen sectors, while its revenue growth earns a strong third place ranking. Revenue growth is reinforced by the recovery of tourism and heightened consumer spending during local festivals, which uniquely boost demand for retail and leisure services in Singapore. The easing of travel restrictions has also increased foot traffic in shopping malls, further supporting sales. [#51O]MSM International Ltd[\#51O] delivered the fastest earnings increase within the group, whereas [#5OX]Mary Chia Holdings Ltd[\#5OX] led the sector in revenue growth.
Transportation & Logistics: Transportation & Logistics delivered modest expansion, with average annual earnings rising 2.62% and average annual revenue increasing 2.65% over the past year. The sector ranked eleventh out of fifteen for earnings growth and also placed eleventh for revenue growth, indicating performance near the lower third of all SGX sectors. Within the group, [#FQ7]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7] posted the strongest earnings acceleration, while [#R14]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14] led the revenue surge. Growth was shaped by Singapore’s continued development of its maritime hub, tighter port capacity constraints, and rising demand for last-mile delivery driven by e‑commerce, all of which uniquely influence logistics operators. At the same time, tighter emissions regulations for freight vehicles added cost pressure, tempering the overall pace of expansion.
Healthcare: Despite a sharp decline in earnings, the Healthcare sector posted an average annual earnings growth of minus 83.91 percent, placing it 14th out of 15 sectors for earnings growth. At the same time, revenue expanded by an average of 18.23 percent, earning the sector the second best rank for revenue growth among all sectors. [#1H3]Clearbridge Health Ltd[\#1H3] delivered the strongest earnings increase within the sector, while [#8YY]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY] led the revenue surge. Growth in Singapore's healthcare market is shaped by the nation's stringent drug approval process, a rapidly aging population that raises demand for specialised services, and recent government incentives for telemedicine adoption that boost revenue opportunities.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector posted an average annual earnings growth of about 80.7%, placing it fourth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion, while its average annual revenue growth of roughly 20.5% ranked it first for revenue increase. [#5IC][#5IC]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC][\#5IC] led the sector, delivering the highest yearly earnings growth and also achieving the top revenue growth within the group. The sector’s strong performance is further supported by Singapore’s limited land availability, which drives premium pricing for developable sites, and by government policies that prioritize high‑density residential and logistics projects, both of which create a pipeline of demand that fuels earnings and revenue gains. Additionally, recent tightening of foreign buyer restrictions has shifted investment toward local developers, adding another boost to sector‑wide growth.
Energy: The Energy sector posted a contraction in earnings, with an average annual earnings decline of 11.48%, while revenue grew modestly by 0.54% over the past year. This performance placed the sector 13th out of 15 sectors for earnings growth and 14th for revenue growth, indicating relative weakness compared with most peers. [#JFQ]JFQ[\#JFQ] recorded the strongest yearly earnings expansion in the sector, and [#BDU]Federal International (2000) Ltd[\#BDU] achieved the highest yearly revenue growth. Growth in Singapore's Energy sector is uniquely constrained by the country's limited domestic hydrocarbon reserves, heavy reliance on imported fuel, and regulatory caps on power tariffs that compress margins. Additionally, ongoing policy shifts toward renewable energy and stricter emissions standards add further pressure on traditional energy operators.
Utilities: The Utilities sector posted a robust earnings expansion of 40.16% on average, positioning it sixth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. At the same time, average revenue fell by 7.36%, leaving the sector at the bottom of the revenue growth ranking. [#5GD]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the group, while [#BEH]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH] recorded the highest revenue increase despite the overall decline. Growth in Singapore’s utilities is shaped by the Energy Market Authority’s periodic tariff reviews, aggressive renewable energy targets and ongoing investments in grid resilience, all of which can amplify earnings while constraining short‑term revenue streams.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 87.17% over the past year, ranking third among fifteen sectors. Its average annual revenue grew by 13.82%, which places the sector fourth in revenue growth. [#CNE]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE] led the sector with the highest yearly earnings growth, reflecting strong demand for early childhood education supported by government subsidies and a growing resident population. [#5EG]Zhongxin Fruit and Juice Ltd[\#5EG] recorded the highest yearly revenue growth, benefitting from heightened health awareness and a preference for locally produced fruit beverages in Singapore. These trends are reinforced by Singapore’s demographic shift toward more families with young children and a consumer preference for convenient, nutritious food and drink options, which uniquely boost the Consumer Defensive segment.
Financial Services: Over the past year the Financial Services sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 12.68% and an average annual revenue growth of 12.83%. This performance placed the sector ninth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth and sixth for revenue growth. [#I49]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49] delivered the strongest earnings expansion within the group, while [#K6S]Prudential PLC[\#K6S] recorded the highest revenue increase. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s role as a regional banking hub, which attracted cross‑border capital flows and encouraged banks to expand wealth‑management services. In addition, the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s progressive regulatory framework facilitated the rollout of digital banking licences, boosting fee‑based income for local institutions. Together, these sector‑specific dynamics helped sustain the robust earnings and revenue gains observed.
Communication Services: Despite a modest 2.87% rise in average annual revenue, the Communication Services sector posted a steep decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of -121.68%. This places the sector at the bottom of the earnings‑growth ranking, 15th out of 15, while its revenue‑growth rank sits at 10th. The sector’s performance is shaped by Singapore’s stringent content licensing rules and the high cost of spectrum allocation, which limit profit expansion for broadcasters and streaming firms. At the company level, [#9VW][#9VW]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW][\#9VW] delivered the strongest yearly earnings growth and also led revenue growth within the sector. These dynamics highlight the contrast between limited revenue uplift and severe earnings pressure in the Communication Services space.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary earnings surge, with average annual earnings growth of roughly 1046.78%, placing it at the top of all sectors for earnings growth. Its average annual revenue grew by about 9.98%, which ranks it seventh among fifteen sectors. [#KUO]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO] delivered the highest earnings growth in the sector, while [#C8R]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R] led revenue expansion. In Singapore, the sector benefits from the nation’s strategic port facilities that streamline export of cement and chemicals and from ongoing government infrastructure initiatives that boost demand for construction materials, while strict environmental regulations shape production practices.
Infrastructures: Despite modest revenue expansion, the Infrastructures sector delivered explosive earnings growth, with an average annual increase of about 350 percent, the second‑fastest among the fifteen SGX sectors. Revenue rose at a more subdued pace of roughly 2.25 percent, placing the sector twelfth in revenue growth rankings. The surge in earnings was led by [#Z74]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74], which posted the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, while [#S59]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59] recorded the strongest revenue increase. Growth is further driven by Singapore’s ongoing expansion of high‑speed broadband networks and the continued development of airport and airline maintenance capabilities, both of which are specific to infrastructure‑related firms. These sector‑specific dynamics, together with the strong performance of the leading companies, explain the divergent earnings and revenue trajectories observed.
REIT: Over the past year the REIT sector posted an average earnings growth of about 33.25%, placing it eighth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at a more modest 5.31% on average, which also earned the sector an eighth‑place ranking for revenue growth. The strong earnings boost was led by [#M1GU]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU], which recorded the highest yearly earnings increase within the group, while [#DCRU]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU] delivered the top revenue growth. Growth in Singapore’s REIT market is shaped by the limited supply of developable land and the ongoing demand for high‑quality commercial and logistics space, which tend to lift rental yields. In addition, the sector benefits from a stable regulatory framework that encourages foreign investment in property trusts, further supporting earnings momentum.
Industrials: The Industrials sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 11.02%, placing it tenth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Its average annual revenue growth was modest at 0.61%, ranking thirteenth for revenue increase. Within the sector, [#5OC]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC] delivered the strongest earnings growth, while [#Y06]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06] achieved the highest revenue growth. Growth is further shaped by Singapore's position as a regional logistics hub, ongoing port expansion projects, and government incentives for smart manufacturing that drive demand for industrial equipment. A tight labour market for skilled technicians also influences the pace of expansion in the sector.
Technology: The Technology sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 37.07% and an average annual revenue growth of 13.44% over the past year. Among the fifteen SGX sectors, Technology ranks seventh for earnings growth and fifth for revenue growth. [#BLU]GRP Ltd[\#BLU] delivered the strongest earnings expansion in the sector, while [#9MT]MetaOptics Ltd[\#9MT] recorded the highest revenue increase. Growth was further boosted by Singapore’s targeted investments in digital infrastructure, including expanded data‑centre capacity and incentives for cloud‑service providers. In addition, the nation’s aggressive push toward a smart‑city ecosystem has heightened local demand for advanced hardware and software solutions, uniquely supporting the Technology sector’s momentum.
